target.title: fix(boundary-safety): guard response reads and UTF-16 truncation
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a boundary safety guard that inventories existing raw UTF-16 text truncation and unbounded response-body reads, then blocks newly introduced production-file violations in changed-file checks.
- Wire the guard into `pnpm check`, `pnpm check:changed`, and package scripts with a baseline so existing debt stays visible without blocking unrelated PRs.
- Fix the shared response snippet helper and representative ACP/MiniMax/provider call sites to use bounded response reads, UTF-16-safe truncation, and byte-capped body-less buffered diagnostics; restore the infra error-body snippet reader's strict byte/char cap contract after exact-head CI caught the conflict regression.

## Origin / follow-up

Follow-up to #97620. That PR fixed one unbounded provider response-read path. This follow-up addresses the recurring root pattern behind the recent boundary-fix cluster by adding a CI guard for new high-confidence response-body and UTF-16 text-truncation bypasses instead of continuing to rely only on one-off call-site fixes.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- #97620 is the direct source follow-up: it fixed one Google Meet Drive export bounded-read path, while this PR adds the guardrail intended to catch the same failure class when future production files change.
- #96264 is the focused MiniMax VLM success-response bound. This PR partially overlaps that call site, but it is broader: it adds the repository boundary-safety guard, baseline identity fix, JSON stdout contract, response snippet hardening, and representative bounded-read migrations.
- The MiniMax VLM success-response cap now aligns with the shared provider JSON cap at 16 MiB instead of introducing a narrower 4 MiB limit. That keeps the fail-closed behavior for oversized provider success JSON while reducing the compatibility disagreement called out by the related MiniMax-focused review path.
- If maintainers prefer #96264 as the canonical MiniMax-only route, the MiniMax hunk here can be reconciled or dropped while preserving the guard/baseline/tooling work that is unique to this PR.

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Recent boundary fixes have repeatedly patched individual channel/provider call sites for the same two failure classes: user-visible text truncated through raw UTF-16 code units, and external HTTP response bodies read without a byte cap. Without a guard, new provider/channel/plugin code can reintroduce the same failure class after the canonical helpers already exist.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause CI/tooling guard for boundary safety regressions, plus small canonical-helper hardening.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local CI/tooling enforcement path and touched helper/call-site regressions. The proof is scoped to repository guard behavior and local `Response` stream boundaries, not remote service availability.
- **Root cause:** The source invariant was missing from CI: new production code could still bypass OpenClaw's canonical UTF-16 and bounded-response helpers even though those helpers existed. A few shared helpers and representative call sites also still contained raw response reads or raw head truncation, so the repository had no enforced contract that new boundary code must use the canonical owners.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This root-cause fix enforces the missing repository invariant at the source: new production code must not introduce high-confidence raw UTF-16 head truncation or unbounded awaited `Response` body reads. `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` scans production TypeScript with the TypeScript AST, compares findings to a checked-in baseline, and fails only on new changed-file violations. It catches high-confidence raw string head truncation and awaited external `Response` body reads while avoiding tests, fixtures, generated/vendor code, Express response writers, hash/protocol slices, and collection slicing. Baseline identity is stable across line-only movement by comparing file/rule/match counts instead of treating line numbers as part of the violation identity. `scripts/check-changed.mjs` runs the guard for core/extension changes, while `scripts/check.mjs` checks full baseline drift.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not rewrite all legacy baseline entries, add new public APIs, change response-size defaults outside the touched MiniMax success path, or modify credentials/configuration. Full legacy remediation and exhaustive taint analysis are out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` is the source-of-truth validator for new boundary-safety violations; `test/fixtures/boundary-safety-inventory.json` is the baseline contract for current legacy inventory; `src/infra/http-body.ts` is the canonical bounded response/snippet helper for core runtime code; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` exposes the bounded response reader to plugin code; `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` remains the canonical UTF-16-safe truncation owner.
- **Patch quality notes:** The guard is intentionally high-confidence rather than exhaustive: it prevents new clear bypasses without forcing noisy legacy cleanup. After the latest conflict repair on current `origin/main`, the baseline contains 228 known entries and can only be rewritten through a full inventory run with `--all --update-baseline`, so changed-file-only runs cannot accidentally replace the repository baseline. Related open PR scan found no open PR already adding these guard rule names.
- **Target test file:** `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts`, `src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts`, `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts`, `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`, `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts`, and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** New raw `messageText.slice(0, maxChars - 1)` text truncation is flagged; `truncateUtf16Safe(...)` is accepted; collection/hash/protocol slices are ignored; awaited `response.json()` / `res.text().catch(...)` reads are flagged; Express `res.json({...})` writers are ignored; narrow `boundary-safety-ignore` comments before awaited reads are accepted; a baseline-known finding remains accepted when only its line number moves; `--json` mode keeps stdout parseable while routing human status text to stderr; `--update-baseline` fails unless `--all` is present; diagnostic snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams; body-less buffered Response-like diagnostics are preserved under the byte cap; MiniMax tests now exercise real `Response` bodies for bounded JSON reads and prove a 5 MiB success JSON succeeds under the shared 16 MiB cap while a body over 16 MiB is canceled and rejected.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The guard uses a baseline plus changed-file enforcement instead of a broad rewrite, so the test guardrail proves the invariant for new code while leaving legacy entries visible but non-blocking. It intentionally covers only high-confidence AST patterns and explains patch quality warnings from default returns/catches as fail-closed parser branches, not runtime fallbacks that mask user behavior.

## Root Cause

The root cause is a missing repository-level source invariant for boundary code. User-visible text can still be shortened with raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing, which can leave dangling surrogate halves when the cut lands inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character. Remote HTTP responses can still be read with `response.json()`, `response.text()`, or `response.arrayBuffer()` directly, which buffers the entire body before OpenClaw can enforce the intended byte budget.

The canonical helpers existed, but the repository did not have a changed-file guard that forced new production code toward those helpers. As a result, each fix landed as a local call-site patch, while the next integration change could reintroduce the same boundary bypass in a sibling area. The shared response snippet path also still carried a raw no-stream fallback and raw character slicing, so even helper consumers were not fully protected.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** New production code that bypasses UTF-16-safe text truncation or bounded response-body helpers is now caught by the changed-file guard, while existing legacy findings remain tracked in a full-repo baseline. MiniMax VLM success JSON now uses the same bounded provider JSON reader with a 16 MiB cap, preserving normal provider-sized success responses while rejecting/canceling oversized bodies. After the latest repair, the shared snippet path cancels exact-cap diagnostic reads and preserves body-less buffered Response-like diagnostics under `maxBytes` without adding a changed-file boundary-safety violation.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw repair worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774`, branch `repair/pr-97774`, after syncing PR #97774 onto current `origin/main`. - **Observed result after fix:** The full guard baseline matches 228 known legacy entries on the synced repair worktree, while the changed-file guard passes because the patch itself introduces no new unbaseline-known violations. Baseline rewrites now require `--all --update-baseline`, preventing a changed-file-only inventory from replacing the full baseline. The Round 2 conflict repair restores `readResponseBodySnippet`'s strict contract: body-less `Response.text()` compatibility returns/truncates text instead of `""`, byte caps are enforced before char caps, incomplete trailing UTF-8 is dropped at the byte boundary, and no diagnostic ellipsis is appended past `maxBytes` / `maxChars`. The focused test suite verifies UTF-16-safe snippet/progress truncation, bounded response reads, body-less buffered Response-like diagnostics under `maxBytes`, JSON stdout behavior, line-shift-stable baseline identity, MiniMax success JSON acceptance below 16 MiB, MiniMax oversized-body cancellation above 16 MiB, and exact-cap diagnostic snippet cancellation.
- **What was not tested:** No browser UI, hosted CI run, or remote MiniMax availability is claimed. Remote MiniMax is not required to prove this patch because the changed behavior is the local fetch/`Response` body boundary, which is exercised with real `Response` streams. `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and full `pnpm lint --threads=8` were not completed locally for this Round 2 update; the focused changed-file oxlint check passed, and the remaining remote `check-lint` failure was attributed to the current CI base rather than this PR head.

- **Proof request / real behavior evidence:** The reviewer-facing proof is mapped to the actual behavior changed here: repository guard execution, baseline diffing, and local `Response` / Response-like body boundary handling. No browser UI, hosted CI rerun, or remote MiniMax availability is claimed.
- **RF-001 — guard gate / baseline-drift risk:** The guard remains intentionally high-confidence and baseline-backed. Current-head proof shows the full baseline matches 228 entries after syncing with `origin/main`, changed-file guard behavior is still covered by tests, and baseline rewrites now require `--all --update-baseline` so a changed-file-only run cannot replace the repository baseline. Remaining policy acceptance for this CI gate is disclosed as maintainer-review territory.
- **RF-002 — MiniMax >16 MiB compatibility:** The MiniMax success path remains aligned to the shared 16 MiB provider JSON cap. Responses above that cap fail closed instead of fully buffering; this compatibility choice is documented in the merge-risk section and remains covered by the MiniMax boundary tests from the earlier PR proof.
- **RF-003 — changed-file-only baseline rewrite:** Fixed. `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --update-baseline` now returns 1 unless `--all` is also present, and the regression test asserts the baseline file is not written in that mode.
- **RF-004 — exact-head CI completion:** Local proof does not claim final merge readiness. The Round 2 exact-head compact-test failure was reproduced locally and fixed in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts`; the remaining `check-lint` signal was attributed to the current CI base, not this PR head, and final remote status is intentionally delegated to `submit-pr` / `await-pr-settle` after push.
- **RF-005 — narrow automated repair:** Applied only to the baseline update safety path and conflict baseline refresh. The broader guard/cap acceptance questions remain explicitly documented for maintainer decision.
- **RF-006 — full inventory requirement:** Fixed with the same `--all --update-baseline` gate and verified by `node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --all --update-baseline && node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --all`.
- **RF-007 — boundary-safety script tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts` passes with 13 tests on the current repair head.
- **RF-008 — full boundary-safety check:** `node scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs --all` passes with `Boundary safety baseline matches (228 entries)` after the full-inventory baseline refresh.
- **RF-009 — whitespace:** `git diff --check` exits 0 with no output.

## CI follow-up addressed

- **Earlier current-head CI attribution:** The earlier compact-check failures on the previous head were current-PR direct regressions, not stale/main-baseline/infra failures. `checks-node-compact-small-whole-1` failed MiniMax/image-tool tests plus an exact-cap PDF error-body test; `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` failed MiniMax media-understanding tests. Both failure classes line up with this PR's bounded MiniMax JSON reader and response-snippet boundary changes.
- **Round 2 current-head CI attribution:** `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` failed `src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts` because the conflict-resolution wrapper changed `readResponseBodySnippet` semantics: body-less `Response` objects without `arrayBuffer()` returned `""`, and diagnostic ellipsis expansion exceeded strict `maxBytes` / `maxChars` assertions. `check-lint` reported `__escapedBundledSourceLoaded` in `src/channels/plugins/bundled.shape-guard.test.ts` on GitHub's merge commit; that identifier exists in CI base `bf5c9d174822ab916b43288bd06ef97f633209d5`, is absent from PR head `ab3f1a089a56ff1072fe53db116311f1a5ac60aa`, and this PR did not modify that file relative to the merge base.
- **Fix applied:** MiniMax test fixtures now return real JSON `Response` bodies, with fresh bodies for multi-image calls, so the tests exercise the same bounded `Response.body` path as production. Diagnostic text snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams, while `readResponseWithLimit` keeps its success-response overflow semantics. The latest Round 2 repair restores `readResponseBodySnippet`'s body-less `Response.text()` compatibility and strict byte/char cap behavior with UTF-16-safe char truncation, without appending diagnostic ellipses past the caps.
- **Latest focused verification:** After syncing onto current `origin/main`, reran the boundary-safety unit test, full boundary-safety baseline refresh/check, unit-fast routing test, infra response-body tests, changed-file boundary-safety guard, focused oxlint for `src/infra/http-error-body.ts`, and `git diff --check`. Final exact-head CI readiness is left to the submit/settle path after the repaired head is pushed; the known `check-lint` signal is attributed to current CI base state rather than this PR head.

## Regression Test Plan

- `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts` locks guard detection and false-positive boundaries for string truncation, response-body reads, Express writers, collection slices, baseline diffing, line-shift-stable baseline identity, and parseable `--json` stdout.
- `src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts` locks strict error-body snippets: body-less `Response.text()` compatibility, byte caps before char caps, incomplete trailing UTF-8 dropping at the byte boundary, and no ellipsis expansion past strict caps.
- `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts` locks bounded response snippet behavior, body-less buffered Response-like fallback behavior, UTF-16-safe snippet truncation, and exact-cap diagnostic stream cancellation.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts` locks success-response acceptance below the shared 16 MiB cap and overflow cancellation above the cap.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` lock MiniMax callers against real bounded JSON `Response` bodies instead of `.json()`-only mocks.
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts` locks exact-cap provider error-body cancellation.
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts` locks parented ACP task progress truncation without dangling surrogate halves.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** CI/tooling, boundary safety, provider response reads, UTF-16 text truncation, provider compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The guard can block new changed-file code that uses raw response reads or raw string truncation in production files. It should not block unrelated legacy debt because existing entries are baseline-known by stable file/rule/match identity, not by fragile line numbers, and it intentionally excludes tests/fixtures/generated/vendor files plus common false positives. MiniMax VLM success responses over 16 MiB now fail closed through the bounded provider JSON reader instead of fully buffering the body.
- **Why acceptable:** The failure mode is actionable: use `truncateUtf16Safe`, `sliceUtf16Safe`, `readResponseWithLimit`, `readResponseTextSnippet`, `readProviderJsonResponse`, or add a narrow `boundary-safety-ignore <rule-id>: <reason>` for a proven false positive. This turns a repeated review/bug pattern into a local CI failure before PR submission. The MiniMax cap now matches the shared provider JSON response cap, so normal provider-sized success JSON has the same budget as other bounded provider JSON paths.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** This PR does not attempt full legacy remediation, exhaustive taint analysis, or live third-party provider/channel validation.

target.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron jobs that deliver to a configured non-General Telegram forum topic could be marked delivered without Telegram proving the actual provider topic. If Telegram posted to General or another topic, cron delivery state could still look successful because it only had the intended route metadata and message result count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends now surface provider-confirmed `chatId` / `messageThreadId` proof in `meta.telegram.messages[]`.

Core outbound delivery now exposes a generic `validateDeliveryResults` adapter hook that runs after platform send results are available. The Telegram adapter owns the topic-proof check through that hook, so cron no longer re-parses Telegram target grammar. The validator fails closed for explicit non-General topic sends, accepts General topic id `1` without requiring topic proof, and supports username or directory-resolved targets with a separate `threadId`.

## User Impact

Cron Telegram topic deliveries now only count as successful when Telegram's response proves the configured non-General topic. Existing jobs that use numeric targets, topic-suffixed targets, or `@username` targets with a separate `threadId` remain supported.

## Evidence

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`grok-build` is now a real ACPX built-in agent in [openclaw/acpx#426](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/426), merged and released in `acpx@0.12.0`.

This OpenClaw PR consumes that ACPX release and updates the OpenClaw-facing ACP/ACPX/coding-agent guidance so operators can select the real `grok-build` ACPX target instead of treating Grok Build as a docs-only or custom harness path.

Closes #99191

## What Changed

- Bumped the bundled ACPX dependency from `acpx@0.11.2` to `acpx@0.12.0`.
- Updated `pnpm-lock.yaml` for that dependency change.
- Updated ACP docs, ACPX README, and the `coding-agent` skill to reference `grok-build` as the ACPX target.
- Removed the earlier model-selector framing. `grok-build` is the ACPX agent name, not a public model selector.
- Updated ACPX runtime/test coverage for the `acpx@0.12.0` wrapper lease shape:
  - lease identity may be passed through wrapper args rather than env-only;
  - Codex wrapper generic `Internal error` diagnostics still recover the redacted stderr tail through the persisted lease/session identity.

## Why This Shape

The implementation belongs in ACPX, and it has already landed there:

- [openclaw/acpx#426](https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/pull/426) adds `grok-build -> grok agent stdio`.
- The ACPX PR includes live Grok proof with `XAI_API_KEY` and no secret output.
- This OpenClaw PR is the OpenClaw-side consumption/alignment layer: dependency bump plus docs/skill/runtime compatibility.

## Evidence

Current head: `f86e0d1679`


target.title: fix: protect uncovered cleanup window in runCodexAppServerAttempt (#99271)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runCodexAppServerAttempt` has a ~160-line window between turn acceptance and the cleanup `finally` where any synchronous throw leaks notification/request handlers on the shared Codex pooled client, leaves the shared-client lease unreleased, and leaves a phantom active-run handle. This corrupts the session for subsequent attempts and is the structural reason `run-attempt.ts` has the highest fix churn in the repo (219 fix-type commits in 6 months).

## Summary

`runCodexAppServerAttempt` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` had an uncovered exception window: the single cleanup `finally` started ~160 lines too late, leaving every post-turn-accept resource (notification/request handlers, event projector, steering queue, close handler, abort listener, active-run handle, shared-client lease) unprotected against synchronous throws.

### Change

Move the cleanup try boundary from just before `await completion` to right after turn acceptance (line 2938, +0 behavior change), so the single existing `finally` covers **all** resources acquired in the ~160-line setup window.

- Before: only `attachBackend` + `setActiveEmbeddedRun` were try-protected (partial fix)
- After: user-input bridge, projector, steering queue, handlers, close handler, abort listener, reply backend, active-run handle → all covered by one `finally`

## Test plan

- [x] **Inject test** (`run-attempt.cleanup-inject.test.ts`): patches `replyOperation.attachBackend` to throw synchronously, asserts `detachBackend` fires (proves full cleanup path)
- [x] `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts` (8 tests) — passed
- [x] `run-attempt.hooks.test.ts` (21 tests) — passed  
- [x] `run-attempt.native-hook-relay.test.ts` (18 tests) — passed
- [x] `attempt-client-cleanup.test.ts` (2 tests) — passed

## Evidence

**L2 — local vitest inject test** + full regression suite:

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.cleanup-inject.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.8 E:/Projects/skills/work/openclaw
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.hooks.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-hook-relay.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-client-cleanup.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.8 E:/Projects/skills/work/openclaw
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  49 passed (49)
```

Before: `attachBackend` throwing left handlers, lease, active-run handle leaked. After: the expanded try boundary means the `finally` runs `notificationCleanup()`, `requestCleanup()`, `closeCleanup?.()`, `releaseSharedClientLeaseAndRetireOneShotClient()`, `detachBackend`, `clearActiveEmbeddedRun` — every cleanup step fires.

## Root cause

The `try` that owns the cleanup `finally` opened at line ~3107 (`await completion`), but all resource acquisition happened between lines ~2938–3096 — a ~160-line uncovered window.

## Expected vs actual behavior

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Any synchronous throw in setup window | Handlers/lease/active-run leaked | ✅ Full cleanup fires via finally |
| Normal completion | Unchanged | Unchanged |

## Impact

Prevents notification/request handler leaks on the shared Codex pooled client, shared-client lease leaks, and phantom active-run handles when setup fails. No behavior change for the normal (success) path.

## Proof limitations

No live Codex attempt was executed. Evidence is a vitest inject test on the real function with a mock client — L2 (source-repro + inject test), not L3 (live failing attempt).

## Linked issues

- Fixes #99271

target.title: fix(acp): close shared state database on gateway shutdown (#100637)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100637: The standalone ACP gateway process (`serveAcpGateway`) opens a SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection through `createSqliteAcpEventLedger()` but never closes it on SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown. This leaks file descriptors and causes SQLite file locking issues during hot reload.

Additionally, the original fix had an unbounded `Promise.allSettled` drain that could stall shutdown indefinitely if an ACP event handler never settled. This revision bounds the drain with a 2s timeout (matching the gateway shutdown pattern).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/acp/server.ts` | Import `closeOpenClawStateDatabase`; track in-flight `handleGatewayEvent` promises; drain bounded by `ACP_SHUTDOWN_EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (2s) via `Promise.race`; close shared state DB after drain; call `onClosed()` after cleanup |
| `src/acp/server.startup.test.ts` | 3 new tests: DB close on shutdown, bounded drain ordering, stalled-handler timeout (15 tests total) |
| `src/acp/server.shutdown-proof.test.ts` | **Real-behavior proof**: uses real `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` handles (no mocks) to prove `closeOpenClawStateDatabase` releases the underlying handle |

## Evidence

### Unit + proof tests (46/46 pass)

```
=== server.startup.test.ts (unit + drain regression) ===
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)

=== server.shutdown-proof.test.ts (real DatabaseSync proof) ===
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

=== event-ledger.test.ts ===
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)

=== openclaw-state-db.test.ts ===
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Real-behavior proof detail

`server.shutdown-proof.test.ts` exercises the shared state DB lifecycle with **real `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` instances** — the exact same API that the ACP event ledger uses internally. The test:

1. Opens the shared state DB through `openOpenClawStateDatabase` (same path `createSqliteAcpEventLedger` takes)
2. Asserts `db.isOpen === true` and `isOpenClawStateDatabaseOpen() === true`
3. Calls `closeOpenClawStateDatabase` — the core of the ACP shutdown fix
4. Asserts `db.isOpen === false` (proves the underlying `DatabaseSync` handle was actually closed, not just dropped from the module cache)
5. Asserts `isOpenClawStateDatabaseOpen() === false` (proves no cached handle remains)

### Drain timeout regression test detail

`server.startup.test.ts` "continues shutdown after the event drain timeout when a handler stalls":

1. Creates a handler that never settles (simulated stalled `sessionUpdate`)
2. Fires a gateway event → handler begins, tracked in `inFlightEvents`
3. Triggers SIGINT shutdown → hits `Promise.race([allSettled, timeout])`
4. Advances fake timers past 2s → timeout wins
5. Verifies `closeOpenClawStateDatabase` was called (shutdown completed despite stalled handler)

### Diff scope

```

 src/acp/server.startup.test.ts        | 37 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 src/acp/server.ts                     | 18 +++++++++++--

```

target.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses
target.body:
Related: #93425

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators configuring `agents.list[].env` could not rely on that per-agent environment reaching the real subprocess boundary for the configured OpenClaw agent. The gap was most visible when a configured ACP owner such as `reviewer` or `codex-acp` wrapped the shared `codex` harness agent: env lookup, session ownership, MCP inherited env, and ACPX persistent session reuse could follow the harness/raw session identity instead of the configured owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This wires the public `agents.list[].env` contract through the configured-owner source of truth while keeping the ACP harness id as the runtime adapter target. Env lookup, ACP initialization/re-ensure, spawned ACP session keys, subagent allowlist authorization, stdio MCP inherited env, tools-effective fingerprinting, and ACPX persistent-session freshness now use the same configured owner/env boundary.

Security and compatibility boundaries are intentionally unchanged: env injection remains opt-in, host env sanitization still blocks loader/search-path/PATH-style overrides, server-local stdio MCP env keeps precedence for that MCP process, no metadata migration is introduced, `SessionAcpMeta.agent` semantics are not changed, and no new secret provider or ACP protocol shape is added. Because this is a public config surface, `agents.list[].env` values are also marked sensitive for config schema hints/snapshot redaction.

## User Impact

Operators can configure one `agents.list[].env` entry and expect allowed values to reach that agent's real spawned CLI/`exec`, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP subprocess paths, including configured ACP wrappers around a shared harness agent. Blocked env overrides stay filtered, and subagent access still requires the configured owner to be explicitly allowed.

## Evidence

target.title: [codex] Add current OpenRouter image models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related #91504.

OpenRouter image generation currently exposes only a small static shortcut list, so users asking for broader OpenRouter image model support do not see current image-output models in OpenClaw's provider metadata or generated model catalog. Current OpenRouter image models are also documented under OpenRouter's dedicated Images API, so exposing them through the old chat-completions path would advertise models that can fail at runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenRouter's public `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images/models` response currently advertises additional image models beyond the existing OpenClaw list, including:

- `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image`
- `google/gemini-3-pro-image`
- `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image`
- `openai/gpt-5-image`
- `openai/gpt-5-image-mini`
- `microsoft/mai-image-2.5`

This PR adds those current model ids to the curated OpenRouter image-generation provider list, routes them through OpenRouter's dedicated `/images` endpoint, and parses the Images API `data[].b64_json` response shape. Existing preview/default chat-image model refs remain accepted on the chat-completions path so already configured users are not migrated unexpectedly.

OpenRouter `/images` supported parameters are model-specific, so this PR also gates the new models before submission:

- Gemini and Microsoft `/images` models request one output at a time.
- Microsoft receives only supported aspect-ratio/reference-image fields and rejects unsupported resolution requests clearly.
- OpenAI image models reject explicit unsupported Gemini-style `aspectRatio`/`resolution` requests instead of silently dropping them.
- Tool-inferred edit resolution is marked as inferred so OpenRouter can ignore unsupported inferred hints without breaking OpenAI/Microsoft reference-image edits.
- Legacy/default chat-image models keep their previous 5-reference-image guard while current `/images` models can use the shared tool cap of 10 when supported.

This intentionally remains a curated-list update, not dynamic catalog discovery; the broader catalog policy can still be considered separately.

## User Impact

Users can now discover and configure more current OpenRouter image models for the `image_generate` tool without relying on undocumented override strings. The linked issue's `microsoft/mai-image-2.5` example is included. Unsupported model-specific count, geometry, or reference-image requests fail locally with clear errors instead of being sent to OpenRouter and rejected later.

Existing OpenRouter image configs continue to work because the previous preview ids remain in the list and the default is unchanged.

## Evidence

- OpenRouter docs: current image generation uses `POST /api/v1/images` and returns image data through `data[].b64_json`: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/image-generation
- Queried OpenRouter's live `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images/models` endpoint on 2026-06-28 and confirmed the six added ids are present. Live capability proof showed model-specific `n`, `aspect_ratio`, `resolution`, and `input_references` support, including Microsoft `n.max=1`, Microsoft no `resolution`, OpenAI no `aspect_ratio`/`resolution`, and Gemini/Microsoft/OpenAI different reference limits.

target.title: fix(agents): Anthropic-compatible streams hang on oversized partial responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Anthropic-compatible streaming requests could keep accumulating an incomplete SSE frame when the upstream response never sent an event boundary. A malformed or hostile stream could make the transport hang while growing the pending frame buffer instead of failing with a bounded error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic Messages SSE parser now enforces a 16 MiB cap on each pending SSE frame/tail before it continues buffering. Complete event boundaries are drained before checking the remaining pending buffer, so large chunks containing bounded frames are not rejected just because they arrived together.

This does not change provider configuration, request payloads, schema, or normal completed SSE frame handling.

## User Impact

Anthropic-compatible streaming calls now fail fast with a stable transport error when an upstream response sends an oversized incomplete SSE frame. Normal Anthropic streaming responses continue to parse as before.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the new regression test timed out because the stream never rejected the oversized pending frame:


target.title: fix(codex): honor timeoutSeconds for dynamic tool calls when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
Fixes #98864.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tool calls can specify `timeoutSeconds` while omitting `timeoutMs`. `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` previously only read `timeoutMs`, so a tool configured with a seconds-only timeout fell back to the default 90s deadline instead of honoring the caller's intent. The side-question path (`resolveSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs`) had the same gap. Additionally, `timeoutSeconds` was silently floored when a fractional value was supplied, which diverges from the `sessions_send` tool schema that declares `timeoutSeconds` as an integer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` now falls back to `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)` when `timeoutMs` is absent or invalid.
- `readSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` mirrors the main path and also falls back to `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)`.
- Both `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` and `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs` now require `Number.isInteger(value)` and reject fractional seconds instead of flooring them.
- `timeoutMs` still takes precedence when both are present.

## User Impact

Dynamic tools that pass `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. session send helpers) now get the expected per-call hard timeout on both the main dynamic tool path and side-question forks, and fractional seconds are no longer silently misinterpreted.

## Evidence

target.title: improve: enrich exported OTEL logs with stable semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can keep OTEL diagnostic log bodies private today, but redacted records need stable structure to stay useful. This PR makes ordinary `log.record` diagnostics and trusted `security.event` records queryable by event identity and safe structured attributes without enabling broad log-body capture.

The stricter requirement is enforced here: OpenClaw-owned calls that emit OTEL `log.record` now need intentional useful semantics, not only a generic exporter fallback. The remaining non-semantic surfaces are explicit pinned exemptions for console/progress/operator-output callbacks and plugin/free-text forwarding boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostic log export now reserves OpenClaw-owned semantic fields before generic attributes: `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type`, and `openclaw.log.*` event/category/outcome/reason/site attributes. Spoofed generic attributes cannot replace those reserved meanings, and attribute-count pressure cannot drop the semantic fields.

Ordinary logs remain redacted by default. Explicit call-site semantics win when present, subsystem/module/plugin/category metadata fills safe diagnostic semantics, and trusted `security.event` records stay separate from message-body semantics while adding `openclaw.security.<action>` event identity to the existing `openclaw.security.*` schema.

## User Impact

Operators can query exported OpenClaw OTEL logs without parsing message text or enabling content capture. Diagnostic records now carry stable fields such as `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=log.record`, `openclaw.log.event`, `openclaw.log.category`, `openclaw.log.outcome`, `openclaw.log.reason`, `openclaw.log.site_id`, `openclaw.log.level`, and category/source metadata when available.

Security events now use the same top-level event identity shape with `openclaw.signal.type=security.event`, while preserving the trusted security schema. Plugin/free-text logs remain compatible and private: raw message content is not used to infer event names or reason codes, and redacted diagnostic bodies still export as `[message redacted]` unless content capture is intentionally enabled.

Accepted exemption boundary:

- `operator_output_callback: 121` pinned call sites. These are console/progress/operator-output callbacks and are not being converted in this PR.
- `compat_runtime_adapter: 4` pinned call sites for compatibility runtime adapter logging.
- Extension plugin/free-text fallback remains pinned by exact counts and fingerprints: `knownCount=382 knownFingerprint=8ed0750b44745cd1`, `injectedCount=428 injectedFingerprint=695ee489eac02cbb`.
- Plugin logger adapter is not exempt; plugin/runtime logger metadata is wired through the structured logger API and covered by tests.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Redacted `log.record` exports include `eventName`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=log.record`, `openclaw.log.event`, `openclaw.log.category`, `openclaw.log.outcome`, `openclaw.log.reason`, and `openclaw.log.site_id` while keeping the body redacted.
- Capture-enabled `log.record` exports keep the same event identity and semantic attributes while replacing only the body with the log message. This mode is tested only to prove conditional body behavior; it is not required or recommended for normal operation.
- Trusted `security.event` exports include `eventName=openclaw.security.<action>`, `otel.event.name`, `openclaw.signal.type=security.event`, `body=openclaw.security.event`, and the existing `openclaw.security.*` fields.
- Exporter tests prove generic attributes cannot spoof reserved semantic keys or the trusted `openclaw.security.*` event namespace.
- `src/logging/diagnostic-log-site-inventory.test.ts` audits OpenClaw-owned log sites across `src`, `extensions`, `packages`, and `ui`, and fails if owned OTEL-emitting logs lose explicit semantics or if pinned exemptions drift.

Representative exported shapes:

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:...] from wiping archive content
target.body:
<!--
Closes #98241
Related PR: #98246 (same root cause, similar approach)
-->

## Summary

**Problem**: Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` text (pasted log lines, user-typed `[cron:` prefix) silently wipes all prior archive content from `memory_search`. The content-based cron heuristic (`isGeneratedCronPromptMessage`) was previously unguarded — it could fire on ANY user message.

**Solution**: Add two additive guards to restrict when the content-based heuristic fires: `!sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron` (respect session-store classification) and `!hasSeenPriorUserMessage` (only classify first user message as cron). Genuine cron-run transcripts always start with the cron prompt as the very first message.

**What changed**: Added `sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron` and `hasSeenPriorUserMessage` guards to the cron classification block in `buildSessionEntry`. Updated the `keep-cron-run-deleted-archives-opaque` test to include realistic `sessionKey` record metadata. Added a test proving nested `data.sessionKey` provenance is correctly detected.

**What did NOT change**: Record-level `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` check preserved. `sanitizeSessionText` still sanitizes `[cron:...]` messages from rendered content. All existing cron archive behavior is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent data loss: users who paste cron log output or type `[cron:` mid-conversation lose all earlier archive history from `memory_search`. The old unguarded content heuristic matched ANY user message starting with `[cron:...]`, not just the first.

## Root Cause

The content-based heuristic `isGeneratedCronPromptMessage` had only `!generatedByCronRun` as a guard. Since `generatedByCronRun` was set to true on the first cron-pattern match and never reset, subsequent matches were prevented — but if the first match occurred mid-transcript, ALL prior content was wiped. A single human `[cron:...]` message could destroy the entire archive history.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite (40 tests, all pass)

```bash

```

```text
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > first-turn [cron:...] after reset: known scope decision — behaves as cron
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron archive opaque when records carry nested data.sessionKey provenance
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > strips inbound metadata
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > skips inter-session user messages

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

### 2. Multi-scenario verification (5 scenarios, production code path)

The `buildSessionEntry` function was called with realistic archive data covering all relevant edge cases. This is the exact same function the gateway calls during memory sync — no mocks, no stubs, built from the same TypeScript source compiled into the gateway dist.

**Real environment**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout

```text
MID-TRANSCRIPT: [cron:...] after prior user msg does NOT wipe (THE FIX)

  [mid-transcript] hasFirstMsg=true
  [mid-transcript] hasLastMsg=true
ORPHAN CRON: genuine cron archive stays opaque (no regression)
  [orphan-cron] generatedByCronRun=true
SESSION-STORE-CRON: store says cron stays opaque
NORMAL: no cron text content preserved
SESSION-STORE-NOT-CRON: not-cron store not wiped

      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

| # | Scenario | Expected | Result |
|---|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` after prior user message | Content preserved, NOT marked cron | ✅ |
| 2 | Genuine orphan cron archive (records have cron-run session keys) | Opaque (marked cron) | ✅ |
| 3 | Session store says cron | Opaque via session-store classification | ✅ |
| 4 | Normal session, no cron text | Content fully preserved | ✅ |
| 5 | Session store says not-cron | Not wiped | ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent mid-transcript `[cron:...]` from wiping archive content by restricting content-based cron heuristic to the first user message.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout (same `buildSessionEntry` code path the gateway uses during memory sync)

```text
Records retain cron-run session keys after reset/delete.
Both top-level sessionKey and nested data.sessionKey formats are detected.

FIRST-TURN human [cron:] without record-level provenance
  Remains classified as cron-generated (documented scope decision)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` no longer wipes archive content. Genuine orphan cron archives (with cron-run session keys in records, either top-level or nested in `data`) remain correctly opaque.

**What was not tested**: No real-world integration test against a running Gateway with live memory sync. The `buildSessionEntry` function is tested in isolation using realistic archive data matching the production JSONL format.

## Risk checklist

- **merge-risk: low** — two additive guards, no behavioral changes for archives with session-store classification or record-level provenance
- **Risk mitigation**: Test coverage includes: mid-transcript `[cron:...]` (does not wipe), first-turn `[cron:...]` (scope decision — behaves as cron), nested `data.sessionKey` provenance (correctly detected), and all existing archive scenarios
- **Backwards compatible**: Yes — the guards only RESTRICT when the content heuristic fires, never expand it. All existing classification behavior is preserved
- **Regression risk**: None — all 40 existing tests pass; orphan cron behavior is identical for archives with or without record-level provenance
- **Known limitation**: First-turn human `[cron:...]` in a reset/deleted archive without record-level provenance is still classified as cron (see `session-files.ts` guard comment). This is a maintainer policy choice — trusted session-store provenance would be needed to eliminate this trade-off

## Linked context

- **Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98241 — mid-transcript `[cron:...]` archive content wipe
- **Related PR**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98246 — same root cause, approached via trusted provenance
- **Scoping note**: This PR takes maintainer Option 2 (scoped partial fix) from the review — it fixes the mid-transcript case and preserves orphan-cron opacity. The first-turn edge case is documented and tracked. Maintainers can decide whether trusted provenance is needed before closing the canonical issue.

target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply
updates to a running gateway.
```

Paths 1b and 2b produce the original muted output (identical to the real CLI run in proof 1).  
Paths 1 and 2 show the new prominent warning when version changes — the exact code in the PR diff.

### 3. Focused regression test

Added a test case `"warns about stale gateway when --no-restart and version changed"` to the `updateCommand service refresh behavior` scenario suite. The test mocks `runGatewayUpdate` with `before: { version: "1.0.0" }` and `after: { version: "2.0.0" }`, then calls `updateCommand({ restart: false })` and asserts the log contains:

- `"--no-restart set, but the installed version changed"`
- `"stale module imports (issue #92241)"`
- `"openclaw gateway restart"`
- `"openclaw doctor"`

The test passes with the patched code and would fail on current-main muted output.

### Type check

```text
$ npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
  (no errors — type-safe conditional formatting)
```

### Formatting

```text
$ npx oxfmt --check src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Whitespace

```text
$ git diff --check
```

target.title: fix(sessions): prevent delivery-mirror prompt contamination with adjacent dedup and identity fallback (#99470)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a delivery-mirror assistant entry gets stripped of its `provider`/`model` metadata during session rebuild or side-branch merge, it survives the transcript-only filter and leaks into the model prompt as a duplicate assistant message. In the worst case, the entry loses **all** markers (`provider`, `model`, and `openclawDeliveryMirror`), leaving only `{ role, content, usage }` — invisible to any metadata-based filter.

**Production impact**: 33% of submitted prompts were contaminated (108 of 323 `prompt.submitted` trajectory events, 278 duplicate pairs). Downstream, models conditioned on "the assistant says everything twice" mimic the pattern and emit their answer twice inside a single completion in ~2–5% of long replies — user-visible duplicated content on chat surfaces.

Fixes #99470.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three types of delivery-mirror survivors can appear in the provider-bound prompt after session rebuild, each requiring a different defence:

| Survivor type | Markers present | Caught by |
|---------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Live mirror | `provider: "openclaw"`, `model: "delivery-mirror"` | Existing main filter (Layer 0) |
| Stripped mirror | `openclawDeliveryMirror: {…}` only | **Layer 1** — identity fallback (new) |
| Bare mirror | `{ role, content, usage }` only — **no markers** | **Layer 2** — adjacent content dedup (new) |

**Layer 1 — Identity fallback**: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` on main only checks `role`, `provider`, and `model`. When session rebuild/side-branch merge strips `provider`/`model` from a delivery-mirror entry, the entry becomes invisible to this predicate and survives into replay. Adding an `openclawDeliveryMirror` field check catches these stripped-metadata survivors.

**Layer 2 — Adjacent dedup**: When session rebuild strips **all** markers including `openclawDeliveryMirror`, the bare `{ role, content, usage }` entry is indistinguishable from a real reply to any metadata filter. `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` now collapses adjacent byte-identical assistant messages when neither carries tool calls — this is the only layer that can catch the fully-stripped bare duplicate.

**P1 fix — Native tool_use detection**: In `extractToolCallsFromAssistant()` (`tool-call-id.ts`), the `TOOL_CALL_TYPES` set recognizes `"toolCall"`, `"toolUse"`, and `"functionCall"` but not `"tool_use"` — the native Anthropic API content block type. When `isAdjacentAssistantDuplicate()` calls this helper to guard against collapsing tool-call-bearing turns, native `tool_use` blocks are invisible to the guard. Added `"tool_use"` to `TOOL_CALL_TYPES`.

**Not modified**: Session persistence logic, gateway message broadcast, user-visible transcript display.

## User Impact

Users running agents with delivery-mirror channels no longer experience prompt contamination where duplicate assistant messages inflate token usage and degrade model output quality. All three mirror types (live, stripped-marker, fully-bare) are filtered before the provider sees the prompt. Tool-call-bearing assistant turns are preserved regardless of whether the tool call uses camelCase (`toolUse`) or snake_case (`tool_use`) content blocks.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Delivery-mirror assistant entries of all three types (live, stripped-marker, fully-bare) leak into model prompt after session rebuild

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:

Proof script exercises the full `buildSessionContext() → normalizeAssistantReplayContent → provider-bound prompt` path against all 3 mirror types:
```
Case 0 — Session rebuild contamination path (all 3 mirror types)
  Before normalizeAssistantReplayContent (12 messages — 6 are mirrors):
    [4] LIVE-MIRROR    ← Layer 0 (existing main)
    [5] STRIPPED-MIRROR ← Layer 1 (identity fallback)
    [6] BARE-DUP       ← Layer 2 ONLY — no markers at all
    [9] LIVE-MIRROR
    [10] STRIPPED-MIRROR
    [11] BARE-DUP       ← Layer 2 ONLY

  After → 6 clean messages:
    ✓ 12→6 messages (6 delivery-mirror entries removed)
    ✓ No mirror entries in provider-bound output
    ✓ Tool-use turn preserved

Case 2 — Adjacent bare duplicate collapse (Layer 2 only, no marker)
  Uses bareDuplicate(): NO provider, model, or openclawDeliveryMirror
  Layer 1 CANNOT see this entry → only Layer 2 can collapse it
    ✓ 4→3 messages (bare duplicate collapsed)
    ✓ Real assistant reply preserved

Case 4 — Native tool_use blocks prevent collapse
    ✓ 3→3 messages (tool_use turn preserved)
    ✓ Native tool_use block present

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED — provider-bound prompt is clean
```

**Observed result after fix**: All three mirror types are correctly filtered: live mirrors removed by the existing provider/model filter, stripped-marker mirrors removed by Layer 1 (identity fallback), and — critically — bare marker-free mirrors removed by Layer 2 (adjacent content dedup). target.title: fix(edit): normalize JSON string edits in execute path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where the edit tool silently drops edits when models (Opus 4.6, GLM-5.1) send `edits` as a JSON string. Two cases were broken:

1. **JSON string array** (`'[{"oldText":"a","newText":"b"}]'`) — `prepareEditArguments` correctly parsed this but was **never called** in the built-in execution path (only plugin tools and schema normalization invoke `prepareArguments`).
2. **JSON object wrapper** (`'{"edits":[{"oldText":"a","newText":"b"}]}'`) — some models wrap the array in an object, which the parser silently ignored.

Both cases fell through to validation which threw a generic `"edits must contain at least one replacement"` error, giving the model no feedback about what went wrong and causing retry loops.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Called `prepareEditArguments` at the top of `execute()` so the JSON normalization code actually runs for built-in tool invocations.
- Extended `prepareEditArguments` to unwrap `{ edits: [...] }` wrapper objects, handling a format some models produce.

## User Impact
Models using Opus 4.6, GLM-5.1, or any provider that serializes tool arguments as JSON strings can now successfully use the edit tool. Previously these models would get stuck in retry loops when the edit was silently rejected.

## Evidence

### Root cause: `prepareEditArguments` was dead code
The function was set as `prepareArguments` on the tool definition, but the framework only calls `prepareArguments` for plugin tools and schema normalization — never for built-in tools with required parameters. Moving the call into `execute()` fixes this.

### vitest (26 tests, all pass)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Negative control (pre-fix: prepareEditArguments never called)
Without the `execute()` call, the JSON string normalization path is dead code — models sending stringified edits get a generic validation error.

### New regression tests
| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| accepts edits sent as a JSON string array | `JSON.stringify([{...}])` → edit succeeds |
| unwraps edits sent as a JSON object | `JSON.stringify({edits: [{...}]})` → edit succeeds |
| rejects malformed JSON with clear error | `"{malformed"` → validation error (not silent) |

target.title: fix(voice-call): fix telnyx streaming transcription stt in conversation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound Telnyx PSTN calls went silent because Telnyx requires an explicit `POST /v2/calls/{call_control_id}/actions/streaming_start` command to start WebSocket media streaming. Additionally, Telnyx WebSocket frames are structured differently than Twilio frames and were not being parsed.

Two additional issues were addressed after initial review:

1. **Security (ClawSweeper P1):** The original implementation sent a static, reusable stream URL with no per-call credential. A rogue client that knew an active `call_control_id` could inject fake audio. Fixed in commit 2 by embedding a per-call cryptographic token.

2. **Availability (ClawSweeper P1):** `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` returned `true` based on URL+path alone, not on whether the `MediaStreamHandler` was actually initialized. Fixed in commit 2 to match Twilio's readiness contract.

---

## Technical Changes

### Commit 1 — Core streaming path
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: Supported classic `streamPath` configurations, public URL storage, and stream URL resolution.
- `manager/events.ts`: Injected the classic `streamUrl` into `answerCall` parameters for Telnyx inbound calls (bypassed if `realtime` is enabled).
- `media-stream.ts`: Added support for pluggable WS message parsers and implemented `parseTelnyxMediaMessage()` to decode Telnyx inbound WebSocket frames.
- `runtime.ts`: Registered `parseTelnyxMediaMessage` and configured streaming options when initializing Telnyx.
- `cli.ts`: Updated self-check CLI output logic.

### Commit 2 — Security + availability hardening (addresses ClawSweeper P1 findings)
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: `getClassicStreamUrl(callControlId)` now appends a per-call `?token=<crypto.randomBytes(16).base64url>`. `isValidStreamToken(callId, token)` performs constant-time comparison via `safeEqualSecret` (same utility as Twilio). `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` now gates on `this.mediaStreamHandler !== null`, matching Twilio's readiness contract exactly.
- `webhook.ts`: `shouldAcceptStream` callback now validates Telnyx stream tokens the same way Twilio tokens are already validated — unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades are rejected with `1008 Unauthorized stream`.
- `runtime.ts`: Wires `mediaStreamHandler` into `TelnyxProvider` after initialization so the readiness gate is populated.
- `events.ts`: Fixed `TS2352` type assertion (cast through `unknown` as required by TypeScript for non-overlapping interface casts).

---

## Security Fix — How Token Auth Works

```
answerCall()
  └─ getClassicStreamUrl("CA-xyz")
       └─ generates token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("base64url")
       └─ stores token in Map<callControlId, token>
       └─ returns "wss://example.com/voice/stream?token=<token>"

WebSocket upgrade arrives at /voice/stream?token=<t>
  └─ shouldAcceptStream({ callId: "CA-xyz", token: "<t>" })
       └─ telnyx.isValidStreamToken("CA-xyz", "<t>")
            └─ safeEqualSecret(storedToken, providedToken)  ← constant-time
            └─ true → stream accepted
            └─ false → ws.close(1008, "Unauthorized stream")
```

---

## Evidence

### Runtime proof — Security path (from unit test execution)

Test: `rejects start frames when no stream acceptance validator is configured`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-unvalidated (call: CA-unvalidated)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream without an acceptance validator
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unauthorized stream)
```

Test: `returns wss URL when both publicUrl and streamPath configured and mediaStreamHandler is wired`
```
✓ token is not null
✓ token.length > 0
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", token) → true
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", "wrong-token") → false
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-different", token) → false
```

Test: `Telnyx stream-connect not enabled when mediaStreamHandler is not wired`
```
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → false  (no handler)
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → true   (after setMediaStreamHandler)
```

Test: `handles Telnyx start message and connects the stream`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: stream-xyz (call: call-123)
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1005, reason: none)
[MediaStream] Stream stopped: stream-xyz
```

### Full unit test suite results
```
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.test.ts     (21 tests) 55ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts         (24 tests) 632ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts       (20 tests) 2016ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  65 passed (65)
   Duration  52.31s
```

All 65 tests pass, including the new security and readiness gating tests. No pre-existing tests were broken.

target.title: fix(plugins): fall back to runtime registry when manifest pre-filter cannot match tool allowlist
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #100537 — When `active-memory` is configured with external plugin tools (like `lcm_grep`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_expand_query` from `lossless-claw`), the embedded sub-agent run fails with:

```
No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist
(runtime toolsAllow: lcm_grep, lcm_describe, lcm_expand_query);
no registered tools matched.
```

## Root Cause

In `resolvePluginTools` (`src/plugins/tools.ts`), the `resolvePluginToolRuntimePluginIds` function pre-filters which plugin IDs to load based on manifest `contracts.tools`. It only selects a plugin when at least one manifest-declared tool name matches the allowlist.

When the allowlist contains tool names that are registered at runtime via `registerTool()` but are **not** declared in any plugin's manifest `contracts.tools`, the manifest pre-filter produces an empty `onlyPluginIds` list. The function then returned early at line 1125 with zero tools, **never consulting the runtime registry** where the tools are actually available.

## Fix

Added a fallback in `resolvePluginToolRuntimePluginIds`: when the manifest `contracts.tools` pre-filter cannot match any allowlist entry but the allowlist is non-empty, include all enabled plugins that declare tool contracts. This lets the runtime registry perform the actual tool name matching via `pluginToolNamesMatchAllowlist`.

**Safety**: The runtime registry iteration still applies `pluginToolNamesMatchAllowlist` as a second filtering layer, so only tools whose names match the allowlist are returned. The fallback only activates in the failure case (empty pre-filter + non-empty allowlist).

## Changes

- `src/plugins/tools.ts` — Add fallback in `resolvePluginToolRuntimePluginIds` when manifest pre-filter produces empty results with a non-empty allowlist
- `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts` — Add regression test verifying the fallback loads the runtime registry

## Evidence

| Test suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tools.optional.test.ts` | 69/69 passed (1 new regression test) |
| `attempt-tool-construction-plan.test.ts` | 23/23 passed |
| `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` | 68/68 passed |
| `active-memory/index.test.ts` | 156/156 passed |

**Regression proof**: Temporarily removing the fallback block caused the new test to fail (`expected ["lcm_grep"]` but received `[]`), confirming the test detects the bug on current `main` behavior.

target.body:
## Summary

Adds an additive, opt-in video-frame seam to the realtime voice provider contract on the public Plugin SDK so a realtime voice provider plugin can stream periodic still frames alongside audio when the existing `supportsVideoFrames` capability flag is set. Pure additive, fully backwards-compatible: providers that do not opt in see no behavior change.

This replaces the closed #78810 (which targeted the now-removed `src/realtime-voice/provider-types.ts`); the seam is now applied to the post-rename `src/talk/provider-types.ts` path.

## Changes

- `src/talk/provider-types.ts`:
  - Add `RealtimeVoiceVideoFrameMimeType = "image/jpeg" | "image/png" | "image/webp"`.
  - Add `RealtimeVoiceVideoFrameOptions { mimeType?, captureTimestampMs? }`.
  - Add `RealtimeVoiceVideoConfig { mimeType?, fps? }`.
  - Add optional `sendVideoFrame?(frame: Buffer, options?: RealtimeVoiceVideoFrameOptions): void` to `RealtimeVoiceBridge`.
  - Add optional `videoConfig?: RealtimeVoiceVideoConfig` to `RealtimeVoiceBridgeCreateRequest`.
- `src/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice.ts`:
  - Re-export the three new public types so plugin authors consume them through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice`.
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`:
  - Regenerated via `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`:
  - Unreleased / Changes entry under the existing block.

The capability flag `supportsVideoFrames?: boolean` on `RealtimeVoiceProviderCapabilities` already exists in main and is wired through gateway protocol/server-methods; this PR only adds the runtime seam that bridges register to actually deliver frames.

## Boundary notes

- Strictly additive on the public contract: no removed/renamed exports, no required-field changes.
- Both the bridge method and the create-request hint are optional, so existing audio-only providers compile unchanged.
- The new types are re-exported through the existing `src/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice.ts` facade — no new public subpath, no new SDK entrypoint.
- No core code currently calls `sendVideoFrame`; consumer wiring lands in a follow-up PR (callers gated on `capabilities.supportsVideoFrames === true`).

## Real behavior proof

The seam was validated end-to-end against a third-party `jina-live` realtime voice provider plugin (private repo) running on an installed gateway:

- Provider sets `capabilities.supportsVideoFrames = true` and implements `sendVideoFrame` (Gemini Live BidiGenerateContent inline image part, JPEG, 1 fps).
- Gateway logs after a live test:
  - `[jina-live] setupComplete model=models/gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-latest`
  - `[onAudio frame #1 bytes=7680]` (assistant audio frames flowing back over the bridge as before)
  - Korean transcript: `"안녕하세요, 대현님! 지나예요 🌸"`
- Audio path (sendAudio + onAudio) and tool-call path are unchanged; only the new optional video path is exercised when the provider opts in.

## Verification

- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen` then `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` → OK (baseline hash committed).
- `pnpm tsgo` produces no errors against the changed files (`src/talk/provider-types.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice.ts`); other tsgo errors visible locally are pre-existing in unrelated areas (`src/media/**`, `src/plugins/**`, `src/secrets/**`, `src/plugin-sdk/{browser-trash,file-lock}.ts` workspace dep resolution).
- No build/lazy-loading topology change: only types added.

## Test plan

- [x] Plugin SDK API baseline regenerated and committed.
- [x] Existing realtime voice provider plugins continue to compile without implementing `sendVideoFrame`.
- [x] Third-party plugin can register a provider that sets `supportsVideoFrames: true` and implements `sendVideoFrame` and have audio + transcript continue to work (verified live).

target.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args
target.body:
Related: #3569 
Related: #64721

## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` exposes a TypeBox schema to models in Openclaw where almost everything is `Type.Optional`. However the contract is enforced downstream in `normalize.ts` and `persisted-shape.ts` meaning fields that looked optional become required depending on which `kind` was chosen. The code says at ln 54–55:

> "Spell out job/patch properties for model-facing schema; runtime validation still happens in
> normalizeCronJob* to avoid nested union schemas."

In practice this means that openclaw gets no useful feedback from mistakes. Typical failures seen in testing: emitting the `job` argument as a truncated string instead of an object; supplying a top-level `mode` (valid only for the `wake` action); choosing a schedule kind without its required field (e.g. `kind: "cron"` with no `expr`, or omitting `payload.kind`); and passing `toolsAllow`/`fallbacks` as a scalar string instead of an array. Rejection gives generic error messages such as "jobId required" and "job required" with no field-level detail, so the openclaw doesn't have sufficient information to fix the problem. 

## Why This Change Was Made

I mostly use local Gemma 4 26b Q5 which became  completely unable to amend my cron jobs following upgrade to v6 Openclaw. However this is not simply a local LLM issue as Codex also had difficulties. Codex's greater reasoning power allowed for workrounds but with clearer schema these workarounds and iterative fixes wouldn't be needed.

I see that #3569 reported the same issues and the report was later closed through PR #10776. But #10776 did not address the TypeBox schema. @gerroon reported that fails still happen on their Qwen-30b-Instruct after the fix.

Also #64721 reports the same kind of problem: `payload.model`, `payload.timeoutSeconds`,
`payload.contextTokens`, and `maxSpendUsd` are accepted at runtime but the schema rejects
them as unexpected properties.

 Fix could be with a discriminated union, making the model reason about nested conditional types. However my concern is that lower-reasoning local LLMs will not manage this reasoning adequately.

Therefore instead the patch adds a flat top-level field set as an alternative to the nested `job` object:

| Field           | Type    | Notes                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | string  | job name                                       |
| `enabled`       | boolean |                                                |
| `sessionTarget` | string  | `main \| isolated \| current \| session:<id>`  |
| `at`            | string  | ISO-8601, one-shot                             |
| `everyMs`       | integer | recurring interval in ms                       |
| `expr`          | string  | cron expression                                |
| `tz`            | string  | IANA timezone for `expr`                       |
| `message`       | string  | agentTurn prompt — implies `agentTurn` payload |
| `anchorMs`      | integer | start anchor for `everyMs` schedules           |
| `model`         | string  | agentTurn model override                       |
| `fallbacks`     | string[]| agentTurn fallback models                      |
| `toolsAllow`    | string[]| agentTurn allowed tool ids                     |
| `thinking`      | string  | agentTurn thinking override                    |
| `timeoutSeconds`| number  | agentTurn timeout override                     |

The canonicalizer (`cron-tool-canonicalize.ts`) infers `schedule.kind` and `payload.kind` from whichever fields are present, so the model never has to deal with the nested union. Also
descriptions for `text` (implies `systemEvent`) and `mode` (wake only, not delivery mode)
have been tightened up.

The implementation now also normalises scalar toolsAllow / fallbacks into arrays and reconstructs job / patch from recoverable flat fields when the request is clearly a cron add/update call.  This deals with an issue found in testing where openclaw incorrectly tries toolsAllow as a scalar string, or emits a malformed non-object job / patch alongside flat fields.  

## User Impact

Upstream already recovers flat params at runtime: 
`recoverCronObjectFromFlatParams` in `cron-tool-canonicalize.ts` (with
`CRON_FLAT_PAYLOAD_KEYS` / `CRON_FLAT_SCHEDULE_KEYS`)

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

### Test coverage (7 tests pass, 0 failures)

- drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled
- drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard)
- keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard)
- eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard)
- rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths
- preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts
- falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts

| `src/config/types.agents-shared.ts` | Type definition |
