target.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes Telegram/file outbound delivery for trusted generated `text/html` reports after the attachment is staged into the OpenClaw outbound media store.

PR #87982 allowed generated HTML reports under the OpenClaw temp root, but the live outbound flow loads the original file, copies it to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<uuid>.html`, then the channel adapter loads that staged copy again. The second load no longer lives under the temp root, so host-read rejected it and the Telegram message was silently dropped.

This extends the trusted-host-read HTML boundary to the outbound-staged copy through a **content-bound provenance marker** persisted in the shared SQLite state DB, instead of trusting the staging directory by path alone. Trust is bound to the exact staged bytes and verified read-once at host-read time.

Fixes #90557.

## Design

When `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` stages a file whose source was a trusted-generated HTML path (under the temp root), it records a provenance row in a new `outbound_media_provenance` table keyed by the staged file's realpath, storing the `sha256` + `size_bytes` of the staged bytes (`kind = "trusted-generated-html"`, `version = 1`).

At host-read time, a file inside `<mediaDir>/outbound/` is trusted **only if** a provenance row exists for its realpath **and** the row's `sha256` + size match the bytes that `loadWebMedia` already read. Files under the temp root keep their existing unconditional trust. The provenance row is pruned in lockstep with the staged file by `pruneStaleTrustedGeneratedHtmlMarkers`, wired into the media-store retention pass (`cleanOldMedia`).

Preserved guards (unchanged): regular file, not a symlink, `nlink === 1`, final read still validates text shape and HTML document shape.

## ClawSweeper P1 resolution

Two prior P1 code findings are addressed in this revision (independently confirmed sound by a second-model review, which also flagged the read-once requirement below):

- **Path-keyed provenance bypass** → **content-bound + read-once.** The marker now stores `sha256` + `size_bytes`, and host-read trust is decided by hashing the **same buffer `loadWebMedia` already read** (no second filesystem read, so there is no hash-then-read TOCTOU window). A file whose bytes are replaced after the marker is written is rejected. New regression test: stage bytes `B1` + mark with the real digest, overwrite the same path with different bytes `B2`, assert host-read is rejected with `path-not-allowed`.
- **Swallowed marker write failure** → **propagate.** `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` no longer swallows `markTrustedGeneratedHtmlPath` errors; on failure it best-effort unlinks the staged file and rethrows, so an infrastructure/write error surfaces through the normal media-failure path instead of deferring to a later silent Telegram reload drop. New test asserts the rethrow and the best-effort `rm`.

The trust expansion is therefore provenance-gated, content-bound, fail-closed, and persisted in SQLite (matching the canonical-storage policy; an in-memory allowlist would break delayed/restarted delivery).

## Test plan

```text
pnpm db:kysely:gen && pnpm db:kysely:check          # generated types in sync with the new table
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
```

## Real behavior proof

### Deterministic real-code-path before/after (2026-06-24)

This exercises the **same production helpers the Telegram channel adapter uses** — `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` (stage) followed by `loadWebMedia(stagedPath, { hostReadCapability: true })` (the second reload) — on two worktrees that differ by **only this PR's diff**:

- **baseline** = `301213a05f` (this PR's merge-base with `main`; temp-root-only trust gate)
- **candidate** = `2dcfc944` (PR head; content-bound outbound provenance)

The driver writes a generated report under the real OpenClaw temp root, stages it into `media/outbound` (which moves it outside the temp root), then performs the host-read reload exactly as the channel adapter does. Environment: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0.

```text
# baseline (301213a05f) — same source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[baseline] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[baseline] staged under media/outbound = true
[baseline] staged outside temp root    = true
[baseline] RESULT: REJECTED — staged reload host-read BLOCKED
[baseline]         LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads

# candidate (2dcfc944) — identical source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[candidate] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[candidate] staged under media/outbound = true
[candidate] staged outside temp root    = true
[candidate] RESULT: DELIVERED — staged reload host-read ALLOWED (144 bytes, sha==source? true)
[candidate] TAMPER CHECK: ✅ replaced bytes REJECTED — LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads
```

This is the exact production silent-drop (`LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads`) on baseline, and delivery on candidate — with the live tamper step confirming the content binding rejects swapped bytes at the same staged path. It is deterministic, runs in seconds through the real `loadWebMedia` gate, and needs no Telegram client, Mantis SUT, or host-read SUT config. This is the staged-reload-with-host-read path the earlier Mantis run did not exercise (its SUT did not propagate `hostReadCapability`, so both lanes bypassed the gate).

### Original production trace + unit-level confirmation

Behavior addressed: when an agent reply emits `MEDIA:/tmp/openclaw/<file>.html`, OpenClaw's outbound pipeline loads the file once (`/tmp/openclaw/...` is inside the tmp root, so trusted), stages a copy to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<file>---<uuid>.html`, and then the Telegram channel adapter calls `loadWebMedia(stagedPath)` a second time. Before this patch the second call rejected because the staged path is no longer under `/tmp/openclaw/`, and the Telegram message was silently dropped. After this patch the staged path is trusted **iff** its bytes match the recorded provenance digest, and delivery proceeds.

Real environment tested: live OpenClaw on macOS 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0, Telegram Bot API channel (polling). The original silent-drop was reproduced 4 times on the unpatched build (#90557). For this PR the patched code path was exercised in the repository test harness, since the CI checkout cannot drive a live Telegram bot end-to-end.

Evidence after fix (PR head):

```text
node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify
# (exit 0 — generated Kysely types match the schema, incl. sha256 / size_bytes columns)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
 ✓ media  src/media/web-media.test.ts (79 tests)
 ✓ media  src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  84 passed (84)
```

Key new coverage:

```text
# Replacement attack (A1): bytes swapped after the marker → rejected
✓ rejects an outbound-staged HTML whose bytes were replaced after the provenance marker (content-bound trust)
# Provenance row records the real sha256 + size_bytes (no hardcoded digest)
✓ writes a trusted-generated-html provenance row keyed by the staged file's realpath
# Marker write failure (A2): propagated + staged file unlinked
✓ propagates a marker write failure and best-effort unlinks the staged file
```

What was not tested from this checkout: live Telegram Bot API delivery, because the CI environment lacks bot credentials. The original silent-drop behavior was verified in production (#90557, 4 reproductions with a `console.error` probe in the installed `dist`); the proof here demonstrates the trusted-host-read gate now accepts the same staged path **only when its bytes match the recorded digest** and rejects a tampered or unmarked staged file. The same instrumented probe can be re-run on a build containing this PR to confirm end-to-end delivery if needed.

target.title: feat(android): per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies
target.body:
Related: #100698

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Android app cannot connect to a gateway fronted by an authenticating reverse proxy (Cloudflare Access-style service tokens): the proxy rejects the WebSocket upgrade before it reaches the gateway, and the app has no way to attach the proxy's credential headers. Operators with that deployment shape are locked out of mobile entirely; a tunnel sidecar is not an option on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds per-gateway custom request headers, injected on the gateway WebSocket upgrade and nowhere else (the gateway WebSocket is the Android app's only HTTP contact — there are no other OkHttp call sites in app code). Design boundaries:

- Headers are credentials: stored in `EncryptedSharedPreferences` alongside the other gateway secrets (`SecurePrefs`, scoped by endpoint `stableId`), values masked while typing and hidden once saved, never logged.
- `GatewaySession` reads the headers through an injected provider at connect time, so edits apply on the next reconnect without re-pairing. Both runtime sessions (operator + node) share the same `SecurePrefs`-backed provider.
- TLS fingerprint pinning (`GatewayTls`) and the pairing/trust flows are untouched — headers are HTTP-level and ride the `Request`, pinning stays on the trust manager.
- A sanitizer (`GatewayCustomHeaders`) drops reserved handshake headers (`Host`, `Connection`, `Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-*`, `Content-Length`, `Proxy-Connection`) and non-printable-ASCII characters — both to protect the upgrade and because OkHttp throws on such characters, which would otherwise let one bad stored entry wedge every reconnect.
- UI is gated behind the existing Advanced controls → Manual connection surface, scoped to the manual endpoint's `stableId` (the same identity the TLS pin and credentials use).

Non-goals: macOS parity (noted follow-up).

## User Impact

Operators can now put their gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or any header-authenticating proxy) and still use the Android app: add the service-token headers once under Advanced controls → Manual. Existing setups are unaffected; with no headers configured the upgrade request is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest` (Robolectric + MockWebServer): the recorded WebSocket upgrade carries this gateway's sanitized headers, a smuggled `Host` stored for the same gateway is dropped (real host preserved), and headers stored for a *different* gateway never appear — the negative cross-scope leak test, using the exact `SecurePrefs`-backed provider wiring the runtime uses.
- `SecurePrefsTest` (12/12): encrypted round-trip, per-gateway scoping, delete-on-empty, reserved/control-character rejection.
- Focused suites run green on both flavors (`:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` and `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest`); `GatewayTls` is untouched.
- `pnpm android:i18n:check` and `pnpm native:i18n:check` pass with the six new strings translated across all 21 locales.
- Codex autoreview of the branch: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Review

This touches the auth/connection surface. Requesting owner + security review from @openclaw/openclaw-secops before merge (security-sensitive per repo policy); please look specifically at the secure-store scoping, the reserved-header sanitizer, and the non-gateway isolation guarantees.

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

target.title: fix(codex): keep message-tool replies final-only
target.body:
﻿Fixes #100153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex-backed source-channel turns using `message_tool_only` delivery could stop after sending a progress/status line through `message(action=send)`. In the observed Telegram turn, the assistant sent a visible "I'll check..." style status message, OpenClaw treated that delivered `message` call as terminal, and no GitHub/web/tool lookup happened afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the existing terminal-delivery behavior for real `message_tool_only` replies, but makes the Codex developer instruction explicit about the ordering contract: complete required tool work first, then use `message(action=send)` for the current source conversation only as the final user-visible source-channel output. It also distinguishes explicit non-source/out-of-band `message(action=send)` calls, which remain ordinary tool work, from sends that target the current source conversation.

No delivery receipt, route matching, channel integration, config, or tool execution behavior changes.

## User Impact

Users in Telegram/Discord-style source-channel sessions should see fewer turns where the agent says it will check something and then silently stops. Codex is steered to do the work first and send one final visible reply to the current source conversation at the end of the turn, while still allowing explicit out-of-band sends to other conversations during the work.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/steipete/peekaboo's releases.

Peekaboo 3.6.0

[3.6.0] - 2026-07-04

Changed

  • Visualizer animations were redesigned around a single "Ghost HUD" design language: one violet accent with red reserved for destructive operations, dark translucent HUD chips, and a shared motion vocabulary. Clicks show a targeting reticle with impact pulses (dashed ring for right-click), typing streams the actual keystrokes into a caption pill instead of a fake QWERTY keyboard, hotkeys press real macOS-style keycaps in sequence, mouse moves and drags trace a glowing comet with press/release rings, scrolls show flowing chevrons with a count tag, screenshots snap viewfinder brackets, and app lifecycle, window operations, menu paths, dialogs, and Space switches render as matching HUD toasts, outlines, and breadcrumbs.
  • Agent-skill documentation now defines Peekaboo as the authority for product and workflow guidance while allowing distributors such as OpenClaw to ship release-pinned snapshots with host-specific overlays.

Fixed

  • Bridge hosts now always return a non-empty decodable error when error encoding fails, instead of surfacing EOF or a secondary decode failure. Thanks @​SebTardif for #211.
  • Snapshot listing and cleanup now propagate lock-open failures instead of treating unavailable storage as an empty snapshot list. Thanks @​SebTardif for #212.
  • Visual feedback now uses one explicit Core Graphics/Accessibility-to-AppKit coordinate boundary, fixing mirrored or offset click, scroll, trail, swipe, window, dialog, capture, annotated-screenshot, and element-detection overlays across primary and vertically arranged displays without applying Retina scale twice; refreshed element detections also retire stale sheets on screens with no new elements.
  • The Sessions window no longer opens uninvited: it is suppressed at app launch, excluded from state restoration, no longer pops up when the running app is reopened programmatically, and the missing-API-key nudge shows it once instead of on every launch. Open it via the status-bar menu or ⌘⇧P as before.
  • Automation services now route visual feedback to the visualizer by default; the wiring was never hooked up, so click, type, scroll, hotkey, swipe, mouse-move, window, menu, dialog, dock, Space-switch, and screenshot-flash animations were silently dropped even with Peekaboo.app running.
  • The typing caption shows the typed text verbatim (that is its job); typing into secure text fields is masked as bullets before the event is persisted or displayed by sampling the delivery focus immediately before every text segment (including Tab-to-password sequences and background typing), and PEEKABOO_VISUALIZER_MASK_TYPED_TEXT=true masks everything for privacy-sensitive setups.
  • HUD chip shadows and glows no longer clip into hard edges: every overlay window gets a chrome margin so gradients fade out naturally instead of getting cut off at the window border.
  • Rapid agent action streams no longer flood the screen: screenshot flashes, scroll chips, mouse comets, and element sheets are throttled, short cursor hops skip the comet, and single-instance overlays (typing caption, hotkey chip, menu breadcrumb, Space indicator, app toast, element sheets) crossfade into their replacement instead of stacking.
  • Element-detection sheets drop window-sized container rects, cap at 120 highlights per screen, and render in one overlay window per screen instead of one window per element.
  • Debug Mac app builds are now signed with a development identity when one is available, so Screen Recording/Accessibility grants survive rebuilds instead of resetting (and re-prompting) on every build; machines without a certificate keep the unsigned fallback.
  • Visualizer overlays now center on their target instead of pinning to the window's top-leading corner, which had offset click feedback by its padding and clipped or truncated HUD widgets.
  • Mouse-trail and swipe visualizations now convert screen coordinates into window-local space with the correct Y-flip, so the paths render along the cursor's actual travel instead of drawing outside the overlay window.

Removed

  • The visualizer keyboard-theme setting (visualizerKeyboardTheme, config visualizer.keyboardTheme) is gone; it only themed the removed QWERTY typing widget and never affected anything else.

## What Problem This Solves

`/thinking high` (and all levels except off) is rejected for github-copilot provider models like `claude-sonnet-4.6`:
```
Thinking level "high" is not supported for github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6. Use one of: off.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Two issues:

1. **Catch-all model reasoning flag too narrow**: In `models.ts`, the catch-all path only marked `o1/o3` and Codex models as reasoning-capable. Claude models served via Copilot's `anthropic-messages` transport also support reasoning but got `reasoning=false`.

2. **Thinking profile resolver missed SDK-registered plugins**: `provider-thinking.ts` only checked the legacy `PLUGIN_REGISTRY_STATE` and bundled policy surface. Providers like github-copilot that register thinking hooks through the SDK runtime plugin path (via `api.registerProvider`) were never reached.

## Changes

- `extensions/github-copilot/models.ts`: Add `anthropic-messages` transport check to catch-all reasoning detection (+4/-1)
- `src/plugins/provider-thinking.ts`: Add fallback to `resolveProviderRuntimePlugin` for SDK-registered providers (+11/-1)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** /thinking high now works for Claude models via github-copilot provider.
**Environment tested:** Node 22.x on Linux

target.title: fix(agents): MiniMax VLM can consume oversized success responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MiniMax VLM image understanding previously parsed successful `200 OK` responses with `Response.json()`, so a malformed or hostile provider response could be consumed without a body-size bound. Non-OK responses were already read through a bounded diagnostic path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful MiniMax VLM responses now use the existing shared `readProviderJsonResponse` owner. That gives the route the same 16 MiB JSON limit, stream cancellation, and parse-error behavior as other provider HTTP consumers while preserving MiniMax Trace-Id context in the error label. The earlier PR-local 256 KiB reader was deleted; one canonical response reader is simpler and avoids a provider-specific limit and duplicate stream code.

Tests now use real WHATWG `Response` objects so they exercise the production body reader. The regression feeds an unbounded successful stream, verifies rejection at 16 MiB, and proves the stream is cancelled without draining indefinitely.

## User Impact

Normal MiniMax VLM responses are unchanged. Oversized or malformed successful JSON responses now fail with a bounded diagnostic instead of allowing unbounded response consumption. No config, request payload, provider routing, timeout, or public API changes.

## Evidence

- Exact rewritten head: `5eec0663b6cdcfc197340b5df4aa1171efd8aa30` on repaired `main` `8ce620f3e675b25111dcbed6d1e124fedd4756a3`.

## What Problem This Solves

`runSshCommand` and the tar-over-SSH pipe transfer in sandbox/ssh.ts attach `data` listeners to child process stdout/stderr streams, but do not attach `error` listeners. If any stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the OpenClaw process.

Add no-op `error` handlers to all child stdout/stderr streams that have data listeners. Stream read errors are treated as non-fatal because the child process `error`/`close` handlers already report the real outcome.

target.title: fix(feishu): refresh client after invalid token
target.body:
## Summary

- Refresh the cached Feishu client when send/reply/card-send sees Feishu invalid token codes `99991663` or `99991664`.
- Retry the failed send path once after the refresh, covering both thrown SDK/Axios errors and fulfilled Feishu error bodies.
- Add regression coverage for invalid-token classification, one-shot refresh retry, and no infinite retry loop.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #97287.

Feishu can return invalid tenant/app access token errors after cached SDK auth state goes stale. Before this change, those responses were treated as terminal send failures, so operators had to manually restart the gateway to clear the cached client/token state.

## Changes

- Add `refreshFeishuClient()` to invalidate and recreate the cached Feishu client for the affected account.
- Extend `requestFeishuApi()` with an optional `onInvalidToken` hook that refreshes once before retrying invalid-token responses.
- Wire Feishu text/card send paths through a mutable client ref so the retry uses the freshly-created client.
- Add focused regression tests for `99991663` / `99991664` thrown and fulfilled response shapes.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts` — 57 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts` — 40 tests passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint extensions/feishu/src/client.ts extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts extensions/feishu/src/send-target.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Diff secret scan — passed.

Note: `pnpm lint --threads=8` was attempted, but the full-repo lint shard timed out locally after 300s while `oxlint:core` was still running; the changed Feishu files were linted directly with oxlint as listed above.

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu send failures with invalid token codes `99991663` / `99991664` no longer require a gateway restart just to clear stale cached Feishu auth/client state. The affected send operation refreshes the account client once and retries with the fresh client, while unrelated Feishu errors still fail fast and repeated invalid-token failures stop after one refresh.

## Evidence

- Regression tests prove thrown invalid-token errors refresh once and retry successfully.
- Regression tests prove fulfilled invalid-token bodies refresh once and retry successfully.
- Regression tests prove persistent invalid-token failures do not loop forever and surface the wrapped Feishu code.
- Duplicate check immediately before publishing found no open PR referencing `#97287`, `99991663`, `99991664`, or the Feishu invalid-token direction.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
125/125 tests pass across 3 test files.

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

---

target.title: feat(diffs): changed-files summary nav for multi-file patch diffs
target.body:
Closes #100673

## What Problem This Solves

Multi-file patch diffs in the `diffs` plugin viewer render as an undifferentiated stack of file cards: no overview of which files changed, no total change size, and no way to jump to a specific file. Rendered PNG/PDF exports also capture the interactive layout/wrap/background/theme toggle buttons, which are dead controls in a static file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Multi-file patches now get an SSR-rendered changed-files summary card — totals, per-file `+N`/`-N` counts, added/deleted/renamed badges, and anchor links to each file card — so navigation works in the hosted viewer and in file exports without extra JS. Per-file counts are computed from the hunk metadata `@pierre/diffs` already provides and match the library's built-in per-file header counts (which is why no per-file header chip was added — the header already shows counts). In image render mode the client now returns no header metadata, dropping the interactive toolbar from captures while keeping the built-in counts. Single-file diffs intentionally get no summary card.

## User Impact

Agents and users reviewing multi-file `diffs` tool output in canvas start with a clickable changed-files summary showing change size at a glance. PNG/PDF outputs no longer show inert toggle buttons.

## Evidence

- Dependency contract verified live against `@pierre/diffs@1.2.12`: `FileDiffMetadata.hunks[].additionLines/deletionLines`, `type` (`new`/`deleted`/`rename-*`), `prevName`, and the built-in header count rendering in `createFileHeaderElement.js`/`createMetadataElement`.
- New tests: summary nav content/anchors/totals, change-type badges, HTML escaping of file names, single-file suppression (`render.test.ts`); viewer-vs-image toolbar behavior and nav-card hydration skip (`viewer-client.test.ts`).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.5) on the change bundle: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Focused `extensions/diffs` suite run via the documented local fallback (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diffs`) because Blacksmith Testbox repeatedly shut down fresh leases during this session; hosted CI on this PR provides the delegated proof.

target.title: fix(voice-call): fix telnyx streaming transcription stt in conversation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound Telnyx PSTN calls went silent because Telnyx requires an explicit `POST /v2/calls/{call_control_id}/actions/streaming_start` command to start WebSocket media streaming. Additionally, Telnyx WebSocket frames are structured differently than Twilio frames and were not being parsed.

Two additional issues were addressed after initial review:

1. **Security (ClawSweeper P1):** The original implementation sent a static, reusable stream URL with no per-call credential. A rogue client that knew an active `call_control_id` could inject fake audio. Fixed in commit 2 by embedding a per-call cryptographic token.

2. **Availability (ClawSweeper P1):** `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` returned `true` based on URL+path alone, not on whether the `MediaStreamHandler` was actually initialized. Fixed in commit 2 to match Twilio's readiness contract.

---

## Technical Changes

### Commit 1 — Core streaming path
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: Supported classic `streamPath` configurations, public URL storage, and stream URL resolution.
- `manager/events.ts`: Injected the classic `streamUrl` into `answerCall` parameters for Telnyx inbound calls (bypassed if `realtime` is enabled).
- `media-stream.ts`: Added support for pluggable WS message parsers and implemented `parseTelnyxMediaMessage()` to decode Telnyx inbound WebSocket frames.
- `runtime.ts`: Registered `parseTelnyxMediaMessage` and configured streaming options when initializing Telnyx.
- `cli.ts`: Updated self-check CLI output logic.

### Commit 2 — Security + availability hardening (addresses ClawSweeper P1 findings)
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: `getClassicStreamUrl(callControlId)` now appends a per-call `?token=<crypto.randomBytes(16).base64url>`. `isValidStreamToken(callId, token)` performs constant-time comparison via `safeEqualSecret` (same utility as Twilio). `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` now gates on `this.mediaStreamHandler !== null`, matching Twilio's readiness contract exactly.
- `webhook.ts`: `shouldAcceptStream` callback now validates Telnyx stream tokens the same way Twilio tokens are already validated — unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades are rejected with `1008 Unauthorized stream`.
- `runtime.ts`: Wires `mediaStreamHandler` into `TelnyxProvider` after initialization so the readiness gate is populated.
- `events.ts`: Fixed `TS2352` type assertion (cast through `unknown` as required by TypeScript for non-overlapping interface casts).

---

## Security Fix — How Token Auth Works

```
answerCall()
  └─ getClassicStreamUrl("CA-xyz")
       └─ generates token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("base64url")
       └─ stores token in Map<callControlId, token>
       └─ returns "wss://example.com/voice/stream?token=<token>"

WebSocket upgrade arrives at /voice/stream?token=<t>
  └─ shouldAcceptStream({ callId: "CA-xyz", token: "<t>" })
       └─ telnyx.isValidStreamToken("CA-xyz", "<t>")
            └─ safeEqualSecret(storedToken, providedToken)  ← constant-time
            └─ true → stream accepted
            └─ false → ws.close(1008, "Unauthorized stream")
```

---

## Evidence

### Runtime proof — Security path (from unit test execution)

Test: `rejects start frames when no stream acceptance validator is configured`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: MZ-unvalidated (call: CA-unvalidated)
[MediaStream] Rejecting stream without an acceptance validator
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1008, reason: Unauthorized stream)
```

Test: `returns wss URL when both publicUrl and streamPath configured and mediaStreamHandler is wired`
```
✓ token is not null
✓ token.length > 0
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", token) → true
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-123", "wrong-token") → false
✓ isValidStreamToken("call-different", token) → false
```

Test: `Telnyx stream-connect not enabled when mediaStreamHandler is not wired`
```
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → false  (no handler)
✓ isConversationStreamConnectEnabled() → true   (after setMediaStreamHandler)
```

Test: `handles Telnyx start message and connects the stream`
```
[MediaStream] Stream started: stream-xyz (call: call-123)
[MediaStream] WebSocket closed (code: 1005, reason: none)
[MediaStream] Stream stopped: stream-xyz
```

### Full unit test suite results
```
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/providers/telnyx.test.ts     (21 tests) 55ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.test.ts         (24 tests) 632ms
 ✓ extensions/voice-call/src/manager/events.test.ts       (20 tests) 2016ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  65 passed (65)
   Duration  52.31s
```

All 65 tests pass, including the new security and readiness gating tests. No pre-existing tests were broken.

target.title: feat: Auto-generate session titles from first user message
target.body:
## Summary

Adds title-based session naming similar to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. After the first reply in a new session, an LLM call generates a concise 3-6 word title (e.g. "Python Array Sorting Help") and stores it as `displayName`, which is what `deriveSessionTitle` returns.

This replaces the current behavior of just truncating the first user message at 60 characters.

## Changes

- **`dashboard-session-title.ts`** — Generalized from dashboard-only to all sessions
  - Renamed functions: `isSessionTitleCandidate`, `maybeGenerateSessionTitle`, `normalizeSessionTitle`
  - Old dashboard-specific names kept as deprecated aliases for backward compat
  - Dashboard sessions always get titles (existing behavior preserved)
  - Non-dashboard sessions require `isNewSession` + `autoTitle` config enabled
  - Uses existing `generateConversationLabel` (no duplication)

- **`chat.ts`** — Extended title generation trigger to all sessions
  - Checks `cfg.session?.autoTitle !== false` (default: true)
  - Detects first turn via `!entry || entry.sessionId !== admittedSessionId || !entry.systemSent`
  - Emits `sessionsChanged` with reason `chat.title` after title is persisted (same as dashboard path)

- **`zod-schema.session.ts`** — Added `autoTitle: z.boolean().optional()` to `SessionSchema`
  - Runtime config parsing now accepts the new key

- **`types.base.ts`** — Added `session.autoTitle?: boolean` to `SessionConfig`

- **`schema.labels.ts`** — Added schema label for the config UI

## Config

```yaml
session:
  autoTitle: true  # default, set false to disable
```

## How it works

1. User sends first message in a new session
2. Agent generates a reply (as normal)
3. **After** the reply is sent, a background LLM call generates a title from the user message
4. Title is persisted as `displayName` on the session entry
5. `sessionsChanged` event emitted so Control UI updates immediately
6. `deriveSessionTitle` returns the AI-generated title instead of raw first-message truncation

The entire title generation is fire-and-forget — it never adds latency to the reply path.

## Addressed Codex review findings

- [x] **P1: Zod schema** — Added `autoTitle` to `SessionSchema` so runtime parsing accepts the key
- [x] **P1: Duplicate implementation** — Generalized existing `maybeGenerateDashboardSessionTitle` instead of duplicating; removed `auto-session-title.ts`
- [x] **P1: Session-change notification** — Title generation from `chat.ts` emits `sessionsChanged` with `reason: chat.title`

## Proof

To verify: send a first message in a new webchat session. The session list should show an AI-generated title (e.g. "Python Help Request") instead of the raw first message truncated at 60 chars.

- **`src/acp/server.ts`** — Call `eventLedger.close()` during ACP server shutdown
- **`src/acp/event-ledger.test.ts`** — Add test verifying close() releases the connection while preserving persisted state

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

### Test coverage (7 tests pass, 0 failures)

- drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled
- drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard)
- keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard)
- eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard)
- rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths
- preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts
- falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts

### Changed files (9 files)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.agents-shared.ts` | Type definition |
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Zod schema with safe-use contract |
| `src/agents/sandbox/types.ts` | `SandboxWorkspaceInfo.skipSkillsSync` |
| `src/agents/sandbox/config.ts` | Config resolver propagation |
| `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` | `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` helper + branching |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.ts` | Name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.test.ts` | 2 new test cases |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | Pass `skipSkillsSync` to sandbox context |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.ts` | Early return guard against host snapshot fallthrough |

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |

| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback now rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait:

- The direct-dispatcher and synthesized-voice paths keep their optimistic queued gating and capture the pre-send final-outcome counts.
- When a captioned final (or its synthesized-voice sibling) is admitted through the raw dispatcher, a post-settlement task is registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` — the same seam the transcript mirror uses. It runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path.
- That task compares the post-settlement final-outcome counts against the pre-send snapshot; if the captioned voice failed or cancelled asynchronously it re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final, so suppressed content is never silently dropped. On success it does nothing, so there is no duplicate text.

This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

Fixes #100637.

## What Problem This Solves

`createSqliteAcpEventLedger()` in `src/acp/event-ledger.ts` opens a SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection through `openOpenClawStateDatabase()` but never exposes a way to close it. During ACP gateway hot-reload or shutdown, the cached handle survives in `cachedDatabases`, causing SQLite file lock contention when the new process attempts to reopen the same database.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Added `close()` to `AcpEventLedger` interface — SQLite ledger calls `closeOpenClawStateDatabase()`, in-memory/API ledger provides a no-op

3. Follows the same lifecycle pattern already used by `plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts`, `task-registry.store.sqlite.ts`, and `task-flow-registry.store.sqlite.ts`

All `AcpEventLedger` implementations now satisfy the lifecycle contract — the in-memory ledger (used by `createLedgerApi()` and `createInMemoryAcpEventLedger()`) has a no-op `close()`, consistent with the interface requirement.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(process): unref closeFallbackTimer to allow natural CLI exit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `src/process/exec.ts`, when a child process exits, `runCommandWithTimeout` registers a `closeFallbackTimer` (250ms `setTimeout`) to force-destroy stdout/stderr streams if they haven't emitted a `close` event. However, this timer is not `unref()`'d, so it holds the Node.js event loop alive and delays natural CLI exit by up to 250ms after command completion.

The sibling `processTreeForceKillTimer` (a few lines above) already calls `.unref()` for the same reason. This fix makes both close-path timers consistent.

Fixes #100662.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `.unref()` tells Node's event loop not to count this timer when deciding whether the process has pending work. If no other timers, I/O, or handles are active, the process can exit immediately instead of waiting for the fallback timer.

## Evidence

### Real terminal output (proof script)

```
$ node _proof.cjs
=== Proof: closeFallbackTimer.unref() ===

Without .unref(): 289ms elapsed (timer holds process)
With    .unref(): 35ms elapsed (process exits quickly)

PASS: unref() allows immediate process exit

=== Consistency check ===
  processTreeForceKillTimer.unref(); // already present in exec.ts
  closeFallbackTimer.unref();    // ADDED by this fix

Both close-path timers now consistently call .unref() to avoid
holding the Node process alive after command completion.

=== Results: 1 passed, 0 failed ===
```

### Source evidence

The `processTreeForceKillTimer` at line ~547 of `src/process/exec.ts` already calls `.unref()`:

```ts
processTreeForceKillTimer = setTimeout(() => { ... }, COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS);
processTreeForceKillTimer.unref(); // ← already present
```

The `closeFallbackTimer` at line 662 was missing this call — now added.

## Merge Risk

Minimal — one-line addition of `.unref()`. The timer callback behavior is unchanged; the only difference is that Node can exit the event loop while this timer is still pending. No existing tests are affected.

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): resolve stable execPath for worker fork to survive Homebrew Node upgrades
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Homebrew upgrades Node (e.g. `node 26.3.0 → 26.4.0`), a running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node`). The local embedding worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with `ENOENT`, silently degrading semantic memory until the gateway is restarted.

## Root Cause

`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts:236` calls `fork()` without an explicit `execPath` option. Node.js's `fork()` defaults to `process.execPath`, which resolves to the real Homebrew Cellar path — not the stable `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` symlink. When `brew upgrade` removes the old Cellar directory, every new worker fork hits ENOENT.

## 🚩 Maintainer decision needed: competing fix #99222

> **Action requested**: This PR and #99222 both target the same canonical issue (#99183) with different strategies. **Maintainers, please review the comparison below and comment with your preferred direction** so we can converge on one canonical fix before landing either.

| Dimension | This PR (#99318) | Sibling PR (#99222) |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategy** | Pre-resolve stable execPath **before** fork() | ENOENT retry **after** fork failure |
| **Design principle** | Prevent — match existing production pattern | Recover — handle failure generically |
| **Platform scope** | Homebrew-specific path resolution | All platforms (retry) |
| **Config surface** | None — transparent to user | None — transparent to user |
| **Risk** | Changes `ensureChild()` to async | Adds retry logic |
| **Code surface** | ~45 LOC source + 240 LOC tests | Smaller |

**Why this PR's approach is sound**:

1. **Matches production-tested code**: The daemon already uses this exact pattern in `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` (merged via PR #32185) — Cellar path detection → stable opt symlink resolution. This PR mirrors that proven approach for the memory-worker fork path.
2. **Prevent > recover**: Stopping the ENOENT before it happens avoids unnecessary worker restart cycles, log noise, and potential state loss on each retry.
3. **Narrow scope**: Only affects Homebrew platforms; non-Homebrew paths return `process.execPath` unchanged — zero regression risk verified by L2 evidence.

**macOS Homebrew proof limitation**: This PR was developed and tested on Linux x86_64, which cannot produce macOS-specific Homebrew upgrade terminal output. The Homebrew-specific resolution logic is covered by unit tests with mocked `fs.access` (8/8 passing, all branches covered). The same `Cellar→opt` pattern has been running in production daemon code since PR #32185 was merged.

**Both approaches are valid and could even be complementary** (pre-resolve + ENOENT retry as a belt-and-suspenders safety net). Maintainers, please comment with your direction:
- **Prefer #99318** (pre-resolve, Homebrew-specific, matches existing pattern)
- **Prefer #99222** (retry, cross-platform, simpler code surface)
- **Combine both** (pre-resolve + ENOENT retry fallback)
- **Other** (please describe)

## Summary

**Problem**: After Homebrew upgrades Node, the running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path. The worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with ENOENT, silently degrading semantic memory.

**Solution**: Pre-resolve a stable Node executable path before `fork()`. When `process.execPath` matches a Homebrew Cellar pattern, resolve to the stable opt symlink that survives upgrades. On all other platforms return the original path unchanged.

What changed: New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper (module-level, exported for testing) with a promise cache. `ensureChild()` made async to call the helper before `fork()`. Re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield to prevent concurrent restart race. New test file with 8 unit tests.

What did NOT change: Public API (`createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider`) signature. Package boundaries — no cross-package imports. Worker IPC protocol. Non-Homebrew platform behavior.

## Change Summary

1. **New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper** — module-level, exported for testing. Detects Homebrew Cellar paths (`<prefix>/Cellar/<formula>/<version>/bin/node`) and resolves to the stable opt symlink. Uses lazy module-scoped promise cache.

2. **`ensureChild()` made async** — calls `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` before `fork()` and passes the resolved path via the `execPath` option.

3. **New test file** — 8 unit tests covering Cellar/non-Cellar paths, versioned formulas, opt/bin fallback, cache behavior, and API contract preservation.

### Files changed

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts` — core fix (+1 import, +1 async modifier, ~45 new LOC)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts` — new tests (~240 LOC)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent local embedding worker fork failure (ENOENT) after Homebrew Node upgrade by resolving a stable execPath before fork().

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (Node v24.1.0 via nvm). Homebrew-specific path resolution validated via unit tests with mocked fs.access. Function returns process.execPath unchanged on non-Homebrew platforms, confirming zero regression risk.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct function call via npx tsx, regex pattern validation, unit test execution, type check. All commands executed on the Linux x86_64 environment.

The Homebrew-specific resolution logic is covered by unit tests (mocked fs.access). Gateway E2E with actual Node upgrade — the fix only changes execPath before fork(); the fork+IPC lifecycle is unchanged. Long-running Gateway with repeated worker restarts — cache test confirms repeat calls use the cached promise.

## Risk checklist

- [ ] **merge-risk**: Low — additive change in a single package (memory-host-sdk), no public API changes, no config changes, no dependency changes. The new helper is an internal detail that only affects one call site (`ensureChild()`). On non-Homebrew platforms the behavior is identical.
- [x] **code change is self-contained**: Yes — ~45 LOC in one file + test file
- [x] **does not affect any public API surface**: Yes — `createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider` signature unchanged
- [x] **does not affect any provider/auth/model/catalog code**: Yes

- [x] **changelog needed**: No — internal implementation detail
- [x] **risk mitigation**: Tests cover all resolution paths; cache prevents repeated fs.access; non-Cellar paths return process.execPath unchanged; no new dependencies introduced; re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield prevents concurrent restart race

## Test plan

|----------|----------|
| Non-Cellar path (Linux `/usr/bin/node`) | ✅ returns original path unchanged |
| Cellar path + opt symlink exists | ✅ resolves to opt symlink |

| All symlinks absent | ✅ returns original execPath |
| Versioned formula `node@22` | ✅ resolves versioned formula; skips bin fallback |
| Cache hit on repeated calls | ✅ caches resolved path |
| API backward compatibility | ✅ provider creation contract preserved |

target.title: fix(agents): keep missing error details out of auth health
target.body:
Related: #100600

AI-assisted: yes. Maintainer rewrite reviewed the full auth-profile failure owner, embedded runner callers, fallback siblings, tests, and provider normalization contract.

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenAI-compatible provider can emit `response.failed` without useful error fields. OpenClaw classified that as `no_error_details`, persisted it as auth-profile health, and cooled a valid API key. Later models on the same provider then appeared to have no usable login even though the credential was healthy.

## Why This Change Was Made

An opaque provider failure is useful for retry and model-fallback decisions, but it is not credential-health evidence. The final implementation keeps that runtime classification and moves the persistence gate into the canonical auth-profile state owner:

- API-key profiles never persist `no_error_details` as cooldown state.
- OpenAI OAuth profiles retain the existing WHAM probe, which can provide independent subscription/auth evidence.
- A WHAM result is applied only if the locked store still holds the exact OAuth access/account identity that was probed.
- Classified auth, billing, quota, timeout, and other failure behavior remains unchanged.

This replaces the earlier provider-name special case in the embedded runner. Checking the credential type at the auth-state boundary also handles OpenAI API keys correctly; they cannot use the OAuth-only WHAM contract.

## User Impact

Valid API-key profiles remain immediately reusable after an upstream detail-less failure. The existing replay-safe retry and configured model fallback still run, while OpenAI OAuth health keeps its evidence-backed WHAM handling.

## Evidence

Final reviewed head: `d867dd5da9c74ca4c51dd5e581a7bc09a018bb93`.

- Sanitized public-network AWS Crabbox, no IAM role, no Tailscale, no hydrated credentials: [focused run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cf53a0be5e58) passed 404 tests across the OpenAI transport, auth failure policy, auth usage/state, and embedded fallback suites.
- Real Gateway + CLI agent proof: [live scenario run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f8bd62367bf5) connected Gateway RPC, sent a real Responses SSE `response.failed` with empty details to the configured primary, retried through the production path, returned `LIVE_FALLBACK_OK` from the configured fallback, and then inspected the persisted auth store.
- Live result: 4 primary requests, 1 fallback request, primary `cooldownUntil = null`, and `failureCounts.no_error_details = 0`.
- The focused and live runs used predecessor head `15081b7c83242a91b6e6f8798ead90f5c3668533`; stable patch-id comparison confirms the four runtime/test files are byte-equivalent after the final main rebase.
- Exact reviewed-head Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox run `tbx_01kwv851c0w1m4es6h3rcn3t06` / [Actions run 28777770596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28777770596) passed 401/401 focused assertions across auth usage, persisted failure state, Responses transport, and embedded fallback.
- Final exact-head hosted [CI run 28779057463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28779057463) passed.
- Fresh exact-base Codex autoreview: clean, confidence 0.84, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Fresh sanitized AWS allocation `cbx_7cd1bc10f4d6` exhausted its 30-minute broker window before returning a usable lease; the late handle was explicitly released and no code ran there. Exact-head Testbox and the prior sanitized live Gateway run cover the behavior.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` passed.

Direct Codex contract inspection confirmed ChatGPT uses `/wham/usage`, Codex API uses `/api/codex/usage`, and only the ChatGPT path style derives from `/backend-api`. No screenshot is included because this is a non-UI persisted-state bug; the structured Gateway run and auth-store result are the direct before/after proof.
